heading: INT. NATURAL HISTORY TAXIDERMY HALL - AFTER HOURS

units.text: INT. NATURAL HISTORY TAXIDERMY HALL - AFTER HOURS
Glass eyes glitter in the dark.
A moth-eaten lion, a mounted heron in mid-strike, a polar bear gone the color of old teeth.
The air smells of camphor and lacquer.
A single green exit sign makes the room look underwater.
CURATOR AUGUSTINE FELLOWES-BAI, 60, gaunt, white gloves, an enormous ring of keys, stands before the heron with his back to the door.
He talks to the bird like an old friend.
Not tonight, old man. Tonight they're coming for us.
units.name: AUGUSTINE

units.text: Heels on marble.
DETECTIVE ZOFIA ARRINGTON, 40s, tailored coat, a flashlight she hasn't turned on, steps through the archway.
Her eyes find him, then the dark, then him again.
Mr. Fellowes-Bai.
units.name: ZOFIA

units.text: Detective Arrington. You are early.
units.name: AUGUSTINE

units.text: I'm on time. You said midnight.
units.name: ZOFIA

units.text: Did I? I may have meant yesterday's midnight.
units.name: AUGUSTINE

units.text: He turns.
His gloves are white.
His hands are not quite steady.
Whoever's behind the display cases, come out now. Slowly.
units.name: ZOFIA

units.text: Silence.
Then, from the diorama of an African savannah, a single glass eye catches the exit light and holds it.
There's no one. Only the animals.
units.name: AUGUSTINE

units.text: Every case has a rear panel. Every rear panel has a latch.
units.name: ZOFIA

units.text: She crosses the hall, tests the nearest latch.
Locked.
She tries the next.
You said you found the first body at nine.
units.name: ZOFIA

units.text: At nine twenty. Under the bear.
units.name: AUGUSTINE

units.text: Who was it?
units.name: ZOFIA

units.text: A boy. Nineteen. A volunteer.
units.name: AUGUSTINE

units.text: Name?
units.name: ZOFIA

units.text: Pellam. Pellam Okonkwo. He cleaned the glass.
units.name: AUGUSTINE

units.text: And the bear is where?
units.name: ZOFIA

units.text: Behind you.
units.name: AUGUSTINE

units.text: She turns.
The polar bear looms in the dark, huge and patient.
She switches on the flashlight.
The beam finds a stain on the floor, scrubbed, but pale.
Someone cleaned this.
units.name: ZOFIA

units.text: I did. It seemed the decent thing.
units.name: AUGUSTINE

units.text: Decent. Mr. Fellowes-Bai, that's called tampering.
units.name: ZOFIA

units.text: Is it? I thought it was called mercy.
units.name: AUGUSTINE

units.text: She sweeps the beam up the bear's shoulder, along the fur, to the glass eyes.
Nobody oils a taxidermy bear's joints.
units.name: ZOFIA

units.text: I beg your pardon?
units.name: AUGUSTINE

units.text: The knees. They're oiled. Look.
units.name: ZOFIA

units.text: She steps close.
The beam picks out a faint sheen, wet, along the hinge of the left hind leg.
Maintenance.
units.name: AUGUSTINE

units.text: At midnight. On a stuffed bear.
units.name: ZOFIA

units.text: We are a very careful institution.
units.name: AUGUSTINE

units.text: Whoever's inside, you have ten seconds, and then I call it in and every officer in the district comes through that door with dogs.
units.name: ZOFIA
paren: raising her voice, for the hall

units.text: Silence.
Then, slowly, with a click of old brass, the bear's chest opens like a cabinet.
Augustine closes his eyes.
Ah.
units.name: AUGUSTINE

units.text: Mr. Fellowes-Bai. What is in the bear?
units.name: ZOFIA

units.text: Everything I could not bury.
units.name: AUGUSTINE

units.text: Of course it is.
units.name: ZOFIA
